speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; can you tell me how long you've had this rash and if it itches worse at any specific time of day?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Dermatitis Herpetiformis.

The chronic, pruritic nature of the rash on the upper extremities over five months in a young adult is highly suggestive of Dermatitis Herpetiformis, which is the cutaneous manifestation of celiac disease.

REQUEST IMAGES: Skin biopsy showing subepidermal blistering with neutrophilic microabscesses.
